the introduction of genomic selection in dairy cattle and sheep has led to a major reconfiguration of the relationships between the actors involved in the process of selection, and that these changes have been accompanied by an effort to maintain the collective nature of selection.
The genomic selection of dairy cattle and sheep is a new technique which is changing the organization of the selection process.

1) the use of genomic data for selection in dairy cattle and sheep is changing the organization of selection activities; 2) this change is occurring in the relationships between actors of the research and actors of selection (development of new public-private partnerships, development of private research dynamics, evolution of historical relationships between public actors and private companies); 3) in the relationships between selection operators (regrouping of operators, questioning of historical cooperation relations due to increased competition and possibilities offered by genomics);
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the organizational changes induced by genomic selection in the French dairy cattle and sheep industries.
the organizational implications of genomics for the French dairy cattle and sheep breeding industries.
the organizational implications of genomic selection in the dairy cattle and sheep industries in France.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genomic selection is a new tool that has the potential to change the organization of the dairy ruminants sector.
